bar.name: v1 HTML fixtures and A2UI for the same apps; 300 blind English requests; independent end-to-end attack on stored rows

biggest_gap: The speed rewrite and positional keys broke things. A line added above a `when` changes its key, so an already-true `when` runs again (points +10 per edit). After any Undo a stale row index shows old values and drops writes through a ref. Catch-up skips real fires.

acceptance.line: >= 90% of 300 blind requests expressible (programs parse and type-check)
acceptance.evidence: mo.mjs check: 330 of 330 OK. Coverage of unseen requests not re-measured.
300 corpus programs: keyword tokenizer median 133, p90 239, max 811.

acceptance.line: every prefix cut at a line end parses
acceptance.evidence: Prefix test passes inside 567/567; fuzz-check 20,000 mutations on a fresh seed: 0 crashes, 0 grammar mismatches.

acceptance.line: edits never lose or retype saved data while marked safe
acceptance.evidence: Stored rows and settings survived. But a safe edit re-runs a true `when` (S1), moves a running timer's state to a timer inserted above it (S2), and an idle timer keeps its old length (S2).

other_notes: S1: after Undo, rowById serves a stale map: taps that write through a ref are dropped and the screen shows undone values (37 hits in 21.5k lockstep steps; 0 in 96.8k once the map is rebuilt).

S2: catch-up stops when one fire changes nothing although the condition depends on time (since, due, windows), and its fingerprint reads only the last row; restore does not migrate old block-state keys; same-named state in two each blocks shares one slot.
All ten round 9 faults confirmed fixed, including the clock and 2,000-row speed (nothing over 200 ms; tick of one day 180 ms). At 20,000 rows a cold screen takes 0.5 to 1.7 s.
